replica_rule: replica r: numpy default_rng(r) bootstrap of the 30 train files (counts in the closed form; theta on the first n_sub distinct drawn files); validation and test fixed
eval_rule: validation and (report-only) test every max(500, steps/40) steps; selection only by validation
title: DBP-X at small Ns + external off-axis triplets (cross rule, closed form)
question: Does DBP-X with Ns = 8 followed by off-axis triplets (cross min(|m|,|n|) <= K, K = 1..3) reach the level of DBP-X Ns = 40 without triplets at the same or lower RM? Also Ns = 4, 10, 20.
dbpx: no training: configuration of E050 start chosen on validation (start_best.csv: sign per Ns from the classical rows, kernel classical or ridge by the lower validation MSE, g, multiplier, complex gain); exact circular filters; DBP-X RM with the honest FIR lengths of E050

triplets.domain: box max(|m|,|n|) <= M, M in (8, 15), cross min(|m|,|n|) <= K, K in (1, 2, 3), merged m <= n, off-axis
triplets.fit: ridge on 30 train files of the DBP-X output, bootstrap counts per replica (5), lambda (6 values) by validation BER
triplets.rm: 12 RM per merged term in both conventions

rm.main: both columns are main: direct convolution (repository convention, model_zoo.macs_phys, symmetric FIR 2(L+1)) and FFT / overlap-save (Xiao 2025 C_conv); the choice of convention is pending (advisor)
rm.note: the linear part of DBP-X replaces CDC in a real receiver; whether it is charged in full is open (author's remark, not decided)

rule_draft.reached: in a given convention: Ns 8 + triplets (mean over 5 replicas) >= DBP-X Ns 40 test value at RM <= RM(Ns 40)
rule_draft.not_worse: gap (Ns40 - Ns8+T) < 2 std and < 2 SE of the replicas (Ns 40 is one deterministic value: no seeds)
rule_draft.limits: no training of DBP-X; one channel, one polarization, 1 sps; files close to periodic (circular filters); spread only from the ridge replicas

value_filter.changes_next_step: yes: decides whether a cheap DBP-X needs triplets or more steps
value_filter.answered_in_literature: Xiao 2025: K = 0 or 1 best on their data (hypothesis here)
